subject: math
title: 3D Objects: Nets, Skeletons, Faces, Edges and Vertices
seo_title: Grade 3 Math 3D Objects Worksheets: Nets and Skeletons (BC Curriculum, Free, Answer Key)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on 3D objects for the BC curriculum: name cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones and spheres, count faces, edges and vertices, find the nets that fold into a cube, count the sticks and connectors in skeletons, and solve real-life word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: A net folds into a 3D object. A skeleton shows its edges (sticks) and vertices (connectors).
key_sub: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Count the faces you cannot see too. A cube net has 6 squares that fold onto 6 different faces. A pyramid comes to a point; a prism does not.
body_html:
What is a 3D object?

A 3D object is solid, like a box or a ball. A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner. Two or more are called vertices. Dashed lines show edges at the back.

ObjectFacesEdgesVerticesReal object
Cube6 squares128a number cube
Rectangular prism6 rectangles128a cereal box
Triangular prism2 triangles, 3 rectangles96a tent
Square-based pyramid1 square, 4 triangles85a pyramid roof
Triangle-based pyramid4 triangles64a pyramid-shaped tea bag
Example 1

How many faces does a cube have?

A picture shows 3 faces. There are 3 more at the back and underneath. 3 + 3 = 6.

Answer: 6 faces

Build with nets

A net is a flat shape that folds up into a 3D object. The net has the same faces as the object. A cube net has 6 squares, but not every group of 6 squares works. Each square must fold onto a different face.

Example 2

A net has 1 square and 4 triangles. What does it make?

The square is the base. The 4 triangles fold up and meet at a point.

Answer: a square-based pyramid

Build skeletons

A skeleton shows only the edges and vertices. Use sticks (like toothpicks or straws) and connectors (like balls of modelling clay). Each stick is an edge. Each connector is a vertex.

Example 3

How many sticks and connectors do you need for a triangular prism?

Edges: 3 on each triangle end and 3 joining them = 9. Vertices: 3 on each end = 6.

Answer: 9 sticks and 6 connectors

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting only the faces you can seeCount the faces at the back and underneath too
Mixing up a prism and a pyramidA pyramid comes to a point. A prism has the same shape at both ends
Thinking any 6 squares make a cubeCheck that no two squares fold onto the same face
Thinking only the cross is a cube netThere are 11 different cube nets
Using the number of faces for sticksSticks are edges; connectors are vertices

faq.q: What do Grade 3 students learn about 3D objects in the BC curriculum?
faq.a: The Grade 3 content standard is construction of 3D objects. Students build objects from nets and as skeletons, and describe their faces, edges and vertices.

faq.q: How many nets of a cube are there?
faq.a: There are 11 different nets of a cube. Each has 6 squares, and no two squares fold onto the same face.

faq.q: What is the difference between a prism and a pyramid?
faq.a: A prism has the same shape at both ends, joined by rectangles, so it has no point. A pyramid has one base and triangle faces that meet at a point.

faq.q: How can I help my child build 3D objects at home?
faq.a: Cut open an empty cereal box to see its net, then fold it back up. Build skeletons with toothpicks and balls of modelling clay, and count the sticks (edges) and balls (vertices).

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too. Do not forget the vertex at the top.

sets.title: Build with nets: which net makes a cube?

items.q: What happens when you fold this net?
c: It makes a box with one face missing.
items.e: The net has only 5 squares. A cube has 6 faces, so one face is left open, like a box with no lid.

items.q: A net is a flat shape that you can fold to make a 3D object. How many squares are in a net of a cube?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, so its net has 6 squares. 8 is the number of vertices and 12 is the number of edges.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face A?
items.e: A and F are in the same line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite faces. Squares that touch in the net are next to each other on the cube.

items.q: Which net folds into a cube?
items.e: B has 6 squares and each one folds onto a different face. A: it has a 2 by 2 block of squares, so two squares overlap; C: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face; D: it has only 5 squares, so one face is missing.

items.q: How many triangles are in the net of a square-based pyramid?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 1 square and 4 triangles. The net has the same faces: 4 triangles.

items.q: Which 3D object does this net make?
items.e: It has 4 triangles. One is the base and the other 3 fold up to meet at a point: a triangle-based pyramid.

items.q: Which 3D object does this net make?
items.e: It has 1 square and 4 triangles. The square is the base and the 4 triangles fold up to meet at a point: a square-based pyramid.

items.q: Will this net fold into a cube?
c: No: a cube net needs 8 squares.
No: two squares fold onto the same face.
Yes: it has a row of 4 squares.
items.e: The 2 squares on top of the row of 4 both fold up onto the top face. The bottom face is left open. Having 6 squares is not enough.

items.q: Which shapes do you need for the net of a triangular prism?
items.e: A net has the same faces as the object. A triangular prism has 2 triangle ends and 3 rectangles.

items.q: Which net folds into a cube?
items.e: D has 6 squares and each one folds onto a different face. A: it has only 5 squares, so one face is missing; B: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face; C: it has a 2 by 2 block of squares, so two squares overlap.

items.q: Which net folds into a triangular prism?
items.e: A: it has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. The others: B makes a rectangular prism, C makes a square-based pyramid, D makes a cube.

items.q: Which 3D object does this net make?
items.e: It has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. The triangles become the ends, so it is a triangular prism. A pyramid net has triangles that meet at a point.

items.q: Which net folds into a cube?
items.e: C has 6 squares and each one folds onto a different face. A: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face; B: 5 squares in a row wrap all the way around, so two squares overlap; D: it has 7 squares, but a cube has only 6 faces.

items.q: Which net will NOT fold into a cube?
items.e: B will not work: it has a 2 by 2 block of squares, so two squares overlap. The other three nets each make a cube.

items.e: It has 6 faces: 4 rectangles and 2 squares. The faces are not all squares, so it folds into a rectangular prism, not a cube.

items.e: C: it has 1 square and 4 triangles that meet at a point. The others: A makes a rectangular prism, B makes a cube, D makes a triangular prism.

items.e: A has 6 squares and each one folds onto a different face. B: 5 squares in a row wrap all the way around, so two squares overlap; C: it has 7 squares, but a cube has only 6 faces; D: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face.

sets.title: Skeletons with sticks and connectors: how many sticks?

items.q: Which object is this skeleton?
items.e: It has 2 triangles at the ends joined by 3 sticks: 9 sticks and 6 connectors. It does not come to a point, so it is a prism.

items.q: Mateo builds a skeleton of a cube. What must be true about the sticks?
c: They are all the same length.
items.e: All the faces of a cube are the same square, so all 12 edges are the same length.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a triangle-based pyramid. How many sticks does it have?
items.e: A triangle-based pyramid has 6 edges, so the skeleton has 6 sticks. Count the lighter sticks at the back too.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a triangle-based pyramid. How many connectors does it have?
items.e: A triangle-based pyramid has 4 vertices, so the skeleton has 4 connectors. 6 is the number of sticks.

items.q: What do you need to build a skeleton of a square-based pyramid?
items.e: Edges: 4 around the square and 4 up to the top = 8 sticks. Vertices: 4 around the square and 1 at the top = 5 connectors.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a square-based pyramid. How many sticks does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 8 edges, so the skeleton has 8 sticks. Count the lighter sticks at the back too.

items.q: What do you need to build a skeleton of a cube?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges (sticks) and 8 vertices (connectors). 6 is the number of faces.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a triangular prism. How many connectors does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 6 vertices, so the skeleton has 6 connectors. 9 is the number of sticks.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a cube. How many connectors does it have?
items.e: A cube has 8 vertices, so the skeleton has 8 connectors. 12 is the number of sticks.

items.q: Which object can you NOT build as a skeleton with straight sticks?
items.e: A sphere is curved all over. It has no straight edges and no vertices, so sticks cannot make it.

items.q: Mei has 8 short sticks and 4 long sticks. She uses all 12 to build a skeleton. Which object is it?
items.e: 12 sticks make a box shape with 8 corners. The sticks are not all the same length, so it is a rectangular prism, not a cube.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a rectangular prism. How many sticks does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 12 edges, so the skeleton has 12 sticks. Count the lighter sticks at the back too.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a triangular prism. How many sticks does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 9 edges, so the skeleton has 9 sticks. Count the lighter sticks at the back too.

items.q: Which object is this skeleton?
items.e: It has a square at the bottom and 4 sticks that meet at a point on top: 8 sticks and 5 connectors. It is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: Leah builds a triangle-based pyramid and a cube. How many sticks does she use altogether?
items.e: A triangle-based pyramid has 6 edges and a cube has 12. 6 + 12 = 18 sticks. 10 adds the faces (4 + 6) instead.

items.q: Wei uses 9 sticks and 6 connectors to build one skeleton. Which object is it?
items.e: 9 edges and 6 vertices: that is a triangular prism. A square-based pyramid has 8 edges and 5 vertices.

items.q: Zara uses 6 sticks and 4 connectors to build one skeleton. Which object is it?
items.e: 6 edges and 4 vertices: that is a triangle-based pyramid. A square-based pyramid needs 8 sticks and 5 connectors.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a cube. How many sticks does it have?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges, so the skeleton has 12 sticks. Count the lighter sticks at the back too.

items.q: You build a skeleton of a 3D object with sticks and connectors. Each stick is …
items.e: A stick is a straight line between two corners, so each stick is an edge.

items.q: In a skeleton, each connector (like a ball of modelling clay) is …
items.e: The connectors join the sticks at the corners, so each connector is a vertex.

sets.title: 3D objects in real life: word problems

items.q: A can of juice stands on a shelf in the fridge. Which part of the can touches the shelf?
items.e: A cylinder stands on one of its flat circle faces. On its curved surface it would roll.

items.q: A box of crackers is shaped like which 3D object?
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces that are not all squares, so it is a rectangular prism.

items.q: On a camping trip, Olivia’s family puts up a tent frame shaped like the skeleton of a triangular prism. How many poles does the frame have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 9 edges: 3 on each triangle end (6) and 3 joining the ends. So the frame has 9 poles.

items.q: A can of soup is shaped like which 3D object?
items.e: A can has 2 circle ends and a curved side, so it is a cylinder.

items.q: Ava makes 2 cube boxes from paper nets. How many paper squares are there in the 2 nets?
items.e: Each cube net has 6 squares. 6 + 6 = 12 squares. 16 counts the vertices (8 + 8) instead.

items.q: Chloe puts one number cube on top of another to make a tower on the table. How many faces of the cubes touch the table or the other cube?
items.e: The bottom cube touches the table with 1 face. The two cubes touch each other with 1 face each: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

items.q: A hockey puck is shaped like which 3D object?
items.e: A puck has 2 flat circle faces and a curved side, so it is a short cylinder.

items.q: Sofia paints a box for a recycling project. She paints every face except the bottom. How many faces does she paint?
items.e: A box has 6 faces. All but the bottom: 6 − 1 = 5 faces. 3 is only the faces you see from the front.

items.q: A tea bag is shaped like a pyramid with 4 triangle faces. Which 3D object is it?
items.e: 4 triangle faces: 1 triangle base and 3 triangles that meet at a point. That is a triangle-based pyramid.

items.q: A tent at a campsite in the Okanagan has a triangle at each end. Which 3D object is it shaped like?
items.e: 2 triangle ends joined by rectangles make a triangular prism. It does not come to one point, so it is not a pyramid.

items.q: Why do stores stack boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, not balls?
c: Flat faces stack with no gaps.
items.e: Rectangular prisms have flat faces, so they sit on top of each other on a shelf. Spheres would roll off.

items.q: A number cube (a die) is shaped like which 3D object?
items.e: It has 6 square faces that are all the same size, so it is a cube.

items.q: A soccer ball is shaped like which 3D object?
items.e: A soccer ball is round all over, so it is a sphere. A circle is flat.

items.q: The attic of a cabin near Whistler has a triangle at each end, two sloping roof sides and a flat floor. Which object is it shaped like?
items.e: 2 triangles at the ends and 3 rectangles (2 roof sides and the floor) make a triangular prism. It has no point, so it is not a pyramid.

items.q: Emma has 20 sticks. She builds one cube skeleton. How many sticks are left?
items.e: A cube uses 12 sticks (12 edges). 20 − 12 = 8 sticks left. 14 comes from taking away 6 faces instead of 12 edges.

items.q: A tissue box sits on Ethan’s desk. He can see 3 of its faces. How many faces can he NOT see?
items.e: A box (rectangular prism) has 6 faces. 6 − 3 = 3 faces are at the back and underneath.

items.q: Noah glues a piece of ribbon along every edge of a cube-shaped gift box. How many pieces of ribbon does he need?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges, so Noah needs 12 pieces. 8 is the number of vertices and 6 is the number of faces.

items.q: There are 4 groups in Simran’s class. Each group builds a square-based pyramid skeleton. How many connectors do they use?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 vertices. 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 connectors. 32 uses the 8 edges (sticks) instead.

items.q: Nadia’s class builds 3 cube skeletons for a display in the hallway. How many sticks do they use?
items.e: Each cube needs 12 sticks. 12 + 12 + 12 = 36 sticks. 24 uses the 8 vertices (8 × 3) instead.

items.q: An ice cream cone is shaped like which 3D object?
items.e: It has a circle at the top, a curved side and a point at the bottom, so it is a cone.
